Unlike classification models or regression tasks where the input and output sizes are fixed and the computation is largely parallelizable, LLMs operate as autoregressive generators. This means that generating a single token depends entirely on the sequence of all previously generated tokens. This sequential dependency, combined with the massive memory footprint of model weights and the variable length of user prompts, creates a complex bottleneck in both latency and throughput. To address these challenges, modern inference servers have evolved beyond simple static batching to incorporate sophisticated mechanisms such as continuous batching, Key-Value (KV) caching, prefix reuse, and speculative decoding. In the prefill phase (processing the input prompt), the model performs a large matrix multiplication across the entire input sequence, which is compute-intensive.
